questions.promptText: Which of the following physical quantities is a scalar?
questions.explanation: Scalars have magnitude only; vectors have both magnitude and direction. A. Velocity: has direction, vector. B. Acceleration: has direction, vector. C. Displacement: directed line segment, vector. D. Distance: total path length, magnitude only, scalar. Answer: D.

questions.promptText: An object weighs 30 N on the Moon. Given that the Moon's gravitational acceleration is 1/6 that of Earth's, the object's weight on Earth is
questions.explanation: Mass does not change with location. On the Moon: W = mg_Moon = 30 N. Since g_Moon = g_Earth/6, W_Earth = 6 × W_Moon = 6 × 30 = 180 N. A divides by 6; B fails to convert; D has an extra factor. Answer: C.

questions.promptText: Which statement about a point particle is correct?

options.text: When studying Earth's rotation, Earth can be treated as a point particle
When studying the time for a train to pass through a tunnel, the train can be treated as a point particle
When studying an athlete's high jump technique, the athlete can be treated as a point particle
A point particle is an idealized model

questions.explanation: A point particle ignores size and shape, treating an object as a mass at a point. A: Earth's shape matters for rotation. B: train length matters for tunnel passage. C: body posture matters for high jump. D: correctly describes the concept. Answer: D. y Question 7 — Answer: D e Path length = full circumference = 2πR (scalar). Displacement = start to end = 0 after a complete loop (vector). Answer: D. Question 8 — Answer: D A A: kinetic friction opposes relative motion, not necessarily the object's motion (e.g. conveyor belt). B: only maximum static friction is proportional to normal force. C: when stationary, friction = weight regardless of grip. D: the foot does not slide on the ground — static friction propels walking. Answer: D.
